note: How a venture's customer problems are ranked (EE-219), and the rules that hold the tree. The weights are unvalidated priors: a venture replaces them under problems in naive.config.json, with the person who set them. Primary, secondary and tertiary are labels on the computed order and are never stored on a problem. packages/naive/src/engine/problems.ts reads this file and packages/naive/src/checks/check-problems.ts enforces the rules.

standards.name: Opportunity solution tree
standards.source: Teresa Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits, Product Talk LLC, 2021
standards.used_for: parent: a child problem is a narrower case of its parent, and the tree is worked one branch at a time

standards.name: Problem tree analysis (Logical Framework Approach)
standards.source: Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation, The Logical Framework Approach, 4th edition, 1999
standards.used_for: cause_of and the core problem: one core problem per profile, with the problems that cause it below it

standards.name: Jobs to be done
standards.source: Anthony Ulwick, Jobs to be Done: Theory to Practice, Idea Bite Press, 2016
standards.used_for: a profile's jobs stay on icp-profile.schema.json jobs; a problem here is a job that is going badly

weights_why: A count of behaviour outranks a count of words, as the evidence grades do (EE-026): money or someone's time already spent on a workaround is behaviour, putting the problem first is a stated ranking, and naming it unprompted is the weakest of the three. The numbers are priors, not measurements.

requires_target.why: A solution, a priced offer and public words about either all claim a problem is worth solving, so the venture names the problem first: the primary profile's core problem, and the one problem it is working on now.
